headline: This law adds Zika virus to the list of tropical diseases that qualify for an FDA priority review voucher program.
what_it_does: The law changes the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act so that Zika virus disease counts as a tropical disease under the priority review voucher program. Under that program, a company that gets approval for a new drug or biological product to prevent or treat a tropical disease receives a voucher. The voucher lets the holder have a future drug application reviewed by the Food and Drug Administration within six months. The law also fixes wording in the list so it refers to filovirus disease, the family of viruses that includes Ebola, instead of the broader family of viruses.

who_it_affects.group: Drug and biologics companies developing treatments for Zika virus
who_it_affects.how: They can earn a priority review voucher if their Zika prevention or treatment product is approved, which can speed review of a later application.

who_it_affects.group: People at risk of Zika virus infection
who_it_affects.how: The program may encourage development of Zika prevention or treatment products, though the law itself does not create any new drug.

who_it_affects.group: Companies developing treatments for filovirus diseases such as Ebola
who_it_affects.how: The corrected wording clarifies that the voucher program's tropical disease list refers to filovirus disease.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on April 19, 2016.
